source_evidence.finding: The raw equation is A_O=((kappa+1)/2)I_n-((kappa-1)/4)(O+O^T). It gives exactly the affine matrix formula used in the proposed algebraic covariance and continuity branches.

The source expressly assumes n>=3 and kappa>=4 and says O is Haar distributed on the full orthogonal group O(n). It calls p_O the density of N(0,A_O^{-1}). Thus full normalized probability Haar is the source object; the source density designation remains a stronger fact than the scoped literal formula theorem.

The source quantifies over every Q in O(n), states that conjugation preserves Haar measure and determinant sign, and explicitly displays A_{QOQ^T}=Q A_O Q^T and p_{QOQ^T}(Qx)=p_O(x). The proposed graph expands exactly these assertions into algebraic and measure-theoretic obligations.

The actual source display equates the signed expectation at x with the expectation at ||x||e_1. The scoped target stops before that display: passing to the axis additionally needs orthogonal transitivity and treatment of zero.

The spatial Gaussian bound and the subsequent explicit invocation of Fubini and Gaussian integration occur after Ex58. They are separate from continuity and integrability over compact O(n) at a fixed x. The later formula shows the expected sqrt(det A_O)/(2pi)^(n/2) prefactor, but neither this nor the source density terminology is a formal Gaussian-law identification in the scoped graph.

node_findings.evidence: Literal Eq4, standing dimension and parameter assumptions, and full O(n) agree with the raw source.

Valid explicit scope definition of a real-valued kernel. The cited source paragraph defines p_O by its Gaussian density designation, rather than printing this entire formula there. Acceptance of R01 is as the declared literal local expression, not a proof that it is that density.

Finite-dimensional real O(n) is closed and bounded in matrix space, hence compact; inherited matrix operations are continuous and the canonical measurable structure is Borel. These are standard implicit bridges, correctly not claimed as additional source quotations.
Orthogonality gives both inverse identities. Conjugation stays orthogonal and conjugation by Q^T is its inverse, including determinant-negative Q.
Matrix multiplication and transpose prove continuity; associativity and Q^T Q=I prove the homomorphism property; inverse conjugation supplies the homeomorphism.
Haar distributed on full O(n) denotes normalized Haar probability. Compactness permits this normalization and gives finite mass one. No SO(n) substitution is supported or needed.

A continuous group automorphism pushes probability Haar to probability Haar: preimages translate under the inverse automorphism, so left invariance and total mass one survive. Uniqueness gives c_Q pushforward mu=mu.
Taking determinants of Q^T Q=I gives det(Q)^2=1. Multiplicativity and det(Q^T)=det(Q) give det(Q O Q^T)=det(O); similarly orthogonal O has determinant plus or minus one.
Expanding Eq4, (Q O Q^T)^T=Q O^T Q^T and Q I Q^T=I give the exact source precision covariance.
Taking determinants in precision covariance cancels the two Q determinants. Applying the same real sqrt to equal determinants needs no positivity or normalization theorem.
Substitution into (Qx)^T Q A_O Q^T(Qx) cancels Q^T Q twice. This is independent of a Gaussian measure or its covariance.
Equal determinant square roots and equal quadratic exponents give literal formula covariance; the fixed denominator is identical on both sides.
All matrix and quadratic entries are finite polynomials in O for fixed x; determinant is polynomial and transpose is continuous.

Real sqrt is continuous on all reals and exp is continuous. Multiplication and division by the fixed scalar preserve continuity. Positive (2pi)^(n/2) follows from positive 2pi and is elementary scalar arithmetic.
A continuous real function on compact O(n) has bounded absolute value and is Borel measurable, hence strongly measurable as an R-valued function. The bound is only for each fixed x.

For each fixed x choose M_x>=0 with |f_x|<=M_x. Then integral |f_x| dmu <= M_x mu(O(n))=M_x<infinity; together with strong measurability this is genuine L1. The universal fixed-x statement also applies at Qx.

With c_Q pushforward mu=mu, the map-integral identity for f_{Qx} yields integral f_{Qx} dmu=integral (f_{Qx} composed with c_Q) dmu. Its hypotheses include actual L1 and Borel measurability, so no default-zero integral convention is being used.
Pointwise determinant preservation multiplied by p(c_Q(O),Qx)=p(O,x) gives equality of the signed integrands.
Replacing the changed integrand pointwise gives the signed fixed-Q invariance with genuine integrals.
Universal introduction over x and Q and conjunction combine L1 and fixed-Q rotation invariance under the declared standing assumptions. No axis map or spatial integral occurs.

scope_boundaries.remaining_obligation: To identify this literal formula with the source Gaussian density one would still need the appropriate Gaussian law, density characterization and normalization, together with precision positivity and covariance identification. None follows from this topology review or is necessary for its scoped conclusion.
To obtain the exact source Ex58 one must construct an orthogonal Q carrying x to ||x||e_1, including x=0. Arbitrary fixed-Q invariance alone does not supply that construction.

Fixed-x L1 on compact O(n) does not imply integrability jointly over O(n) and spatial R^n or justify Tonelli/Fubini for the signed kernel. Joint measurability and an appropriate spatial absolute-integrability or domination argument remain separate.

The axis exponent in U, Ex59's spatial bound, and Ex60/Eq21 integration require subsequent source arguments. Spectral positivity is unnecessary for continuity of the declared real sqrt formula and for conjugation equality.
No determinant cancellation, Poisson/sphere identity, variation estimate, amplification, transcript theorem, eigenbasis result or main lower bound is certified.
